questions.cardText:
[History] Where is the world’s oldest and continually operating institution of higher education located?
A. Morocco
B. Egypt
C. U.K.
Answer: A. The University of Al Quaraouiyine, in Fez, Morocco, founded in 859, is considered the oldest existing and continually operating educational institution in the world.
questions.de: In welchem Land liegt die 859 gegründete Universität al-Qarawiyyin, die als älteste durchgehend betriebene Hochschule der Welt gilt?
questions.en: In which country is the University of al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859 and cited as the world's oldest continually operating institution of higher education?

timeline.labelEn: Fatima al-Fihri founds the al-Qarawiyyin mosque in Fez (857–859), later a leading centre of learning
timeline.labelDe: Fatima al-Fihri gründet in Fès die Moschee al-Qarawiyyin (857–859), später ein führendes Zentrum der Gelehrsamkeit

questions.notes: In Fez. Guinness World Records and UNESCO cite it as the oldest; many scholars note it ran as a madrasa and only became a state university in 1963, so 'oldest university' is disputed.

questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] Which of the following is most likely the smell of a comet?
A. Rotten eggs
B. Rust
C. Ozone
Answer: A. According to the mass spectrometry of the comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, a comet is most likely to smell similar to rotten eggs due to the presence of compounds such as hydrogen sulfide. A comet may also smell like urine because of the presence of ammonia.
questions.de: Nach welchem Geruch würde der Komet 67P/Tschurjumow-Gerassimenko laut dem Massenspektrometer der Raumsonde Rosetta riechen – verursacht durch den Schwefelwasserstoff in seiner Koma?
questions.en: According to the Rosetta probe's mass spectrometer, which smell would comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko give off, caused by the hydrogen sulphide in its coma?

timeline.labelEn: ESA's Rosetta team describes the 'perfume' of comet 67P: rotten eggs, horse stable, formaldehyde, bitter almonds
timeline.labelDe: Das Rosetta-Team der ESA beschreibt das „Parfum“ des Kometen 67P: faule Eier, Pferdestall, Formaldehyd, Bittermandel

questions.notes: ESA (ROSINA PI Kathrin Altwegg) lists rotten eggs (H2S) first, plus horse stable (ammonia — the card says urine), formaldehyde, bitter almonds (HCN), alcohol, vinegar (SO2). Applies to 67P; the card generalises to 'a comet'.
